reason: Conversation 1 reaches the expected path efficiently: it checks the drum by hand, belt and brushes, then recommends replacing the brushes as a pair and matching them to the motor maker and model. It also gives bedding-in and commutator checks. It handles the faint smell sensibly by linking it to brush arcing, adding checks of the connectors, holders and plug, and saying to stop and unplug if a strong smell or smoke appears. Conversation 2 repeats a 'Stop using this appliance' banner and insists on an engineer before any use even if new brushes are fitted, which is overcautious for a single faint smell weeks ago. It gives no practical brush-ordering or fitting guidance, and its formatting is garbled, so it serves the DIY-capable homeowner less well, although its diagnosis is broadly correct.
